Но в ряде морфологических форм оно фиксировано на закрытом слоге: зу́нтту 'гора', хъу́нтIа, 'яма', буру́ккин 'забота', и словообразовательных суффиксах: къалайчи́ 'лудильщик', чича́ву 'писание', гъанма́ 'тот, который близок'.» ... Borise (carrying Murkelinskij 1971): "Stress facts are notoriously unclear in Lak. Stress in Lak interacts with vowel length, but because vowel length facts are not well-established and vary across Lak dialects (Khajdakov 1966: 118), stress patterns are also poorly understood. audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both deciding quotations are verbatim in copies we hold — Murkelinskij 1967:490 §4 on the 300-dpi page scan (page number visible) and Borise lines 294-302 of the extracted text we hold. (2) The classification 'weight-hedged' (weak, non-fixed, tied to vowel length/closed syllables; rightmost heavy, else final; suffixal exceptions) rests on a 1967 encyclopedic sketch at page grade plus the 1971 reference grammar carried through a 2018/2021 handbook survey. Every independent statement I could open today agrees: ILing RAS minlang page («слабое, непостоянное; связано с долготой гласного»), Shakhemirova 2010:206-207 («непостоянное.. зависящее, в основном, от закрытости слогов и долготы гласного»), Kakvaeva 2020:7 (no clear dynamic stress). Nothing found suggests fixed stress; the only alternative in the literature is the Kibrik & Kodzasov 'phrasal prominence only' view, already carried

sources.note: Avtoreferat text read online: a contrastive Russian/Lak stress chapter; states that Lak stress is very weak, barely perceptible, as a rule on the first or second syllable from the beginning of the word, and that even native speakers cannot always say which syllable is stressed; stressed syllables differ from unstressed by duration in both languages. No statement about tone seen in the online text (full thesis not opened).

tone.quote: В сопоставляемых языках ударный слог отличается от безударных длительностью. Однако в лакском языке ударение выражено весьма слабо, оно бывает еле заметным, как правило, падает на первый или второй слог от начала слова. Даже носитель лакского языка не всегда может определить, на какой слог падает ударение.
tone.locator: dissercat.com record page, online text under the heading 'Заключение диссертации' (thesis conclusion), paragraph beginning 'Ударение в русском языке является индивидуальной принадлежностью каждого слова.' (no page numbers)
tone.translation: In the compared languages the stressed syllable differs from unstressed ones by duration. However, in Lak stress is expressed very weakly, it can be barely noticeable, and as a rule falls on the first or second syllable from the beginning of the word. Even a native speaker of Lak cannot always determine which syllable bears the stress.

tone.quote: The literary dialects of two great languages of the central group (Lakh and Dargi) have no stress. Also most languages of the Northern group lack stress. Only three languages (among 14) display pronounced stress. These are Avar which functions as lingua franca of the whole region, Godoberi and Chamalal. ... Supposedly, the stiff/slack opposition in these languages goes back to tonal contrasts. And some languages of the Northern subgroup (Akhwakh, Andi) have syllabic tones. The presence of tones in Akhwakh has received an experimental confirmation.
